title: Generation of mixed murine organoids to model cellular interactions
protocol: Culture mature murine wild-type organoids in 3D in BME2 for at least 7 days in ENR culture medium.
Passage the cultures when the lumen fills with apoptotic cells, approximately once every 3–4 days.
Passage organoid cultures 2–3 days prior to the start of the experiment until mature and healthy organoids are formed.
Harvest organoids by scraping the bottom of the well and pipetting up and down with a p1000 pipette using ice-cold Basic culture medium.
Collect the organoid suspension in 15 mL centrifuge tubes and keep on ice.
Centrifuge at 300×g at 4°C for 5 min.
Use a fire-polished glass Pasteur pipet to mechanically disrupt the organoids.
Pipette up and down 10–20× while pressing the pipet tip against the bottom of the tube, until no clear structures are visible by eye.
Sterilize glass Pasteur pipets by briefly passing them through a flame.
Coat the inside walls of the pipet by aspiration of Basic culture medium.
Monitor the status at a microscope after every 5–10× of pipetting.
Stop breaking organoids before they become single cells.
Centrifuge at 300×g at 4°C for 5 min.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellets in 300 μL ice-cold Basic culture medium.
Prepare one Eppendorf tube for each condition (Pure population A, Pure population B, Mix Population A:B).
Add the correct amount of cell clump suspension according to Table 1.
Centrifuge the mixture at 300×g at 4°C for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully using a p200 pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 μL of ENR medium.
Incubate the Eppendorf vials containing the cell clump suspensions at 37°C for 30 min to promote aggregation.
Do not increase the volume beyond 25 μL during resuspension and incubation.
Dilute the aggregates with ENR medium based on Table 2.
Add double the volume of BME2 compared to diluted aggregates to achieve a final ratio of 1:2, keeping it on ice.
Plate drops of 12 μL per well in an imaging-compatible plate.
Invert the plate and let the drops solidify in a 37°C incubator for 10–30 min.
Carefully add 150 μL room temperature ENR medium per well, do not disrupt the drops, and return the plate to the incubator (37°C, 5% CO2).
Dilute BME2 to a final concentration of 0.8 mg/mL in ice-cold Basic culture medium.
Keep diluted BME2 on ice.
Add 50–150 μL of diluted BME2 per well and incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Wash coated wells twice with Basic culture medium.
Use the plate within 2 hours after coating.
Centrifuge resuspended pellet at 300×g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of TrypLE at room temperature.
Pipette up and down using a fire-polished glass Pasteur pipet to form a single cell suspension.
Immediately add 10 mL of cold Basic culture medium after dissociation is complete.
Keep on ice.
Reduce the incubation time in TrypLE to less than 5 min for organoid cultures sensitive to dissociation.
Process few samples simultaneously and repeatedly monitor until single cell suspension is reached under microscope.
Centrifuge the sample at 300×g at 4°C for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 200 μL of ice-cold Enteroid plating medium to the sample.
Count cells using a Bürker Türk Counting Chamber or automated cell counter.
Dilute and plate cells in ice-cold Enteroid plating medium in an imaging compatible plate according to specific guidelines.
Let the cells adhere in an incubator (37°C, 5% CO2).
Replace the medium with 37°C ENR medium after 16–24 hours.
Refresh the culture medium every 2–3 days.
Start chemical manipulation such as addition of small molecule inhibitors at this stage if necessary.
Add 100 μL Fixation solution and incubate at room temperature for 20 min.
Aspirate the Fixation solution once the drop of BME2 is completely dissolved.
Wash twice with 100 μL PBS.
Add 100 μL blocking solution and incubate at room temperature for at least 30 min.
Add the appropriate primary antibodies diluted in Antibody incubation solution (50 μL per well) and incubate at 4°C protected from light overnight.
Wash three times for 5 min with 100 μL washing solution at room temperature.
Add the appropriate secondary antibodies diluted in antibody incubation solution (50 μL per well) and incubate at room temperature protected from light for at least one hour.
Incubate at 4°C when exceeding 5 hours.
Wash three times with 100 μL washing solution for 5 min each at room temperature.
Rinse twice with 100 μL PBS and leave the organoids in PBS.
Proceed to imaging using a platform of choice.
Acquire Z-stacks for 3D mixed organoids or enteroid monolayers.
Refresh the medium 1 day after plating cells in an imaging-compatible plate.
Add PBS to surrounding empty wells to avoid evaporation.
Proceed with time-lapse imaging using a platform equipped with CO2 and 37°C incubator.
Acquire images with a maximum time interval of one hour and a maximum Z-slice thickness of 5 μm for single cell tracking in 3D.
Harvest organoids by scraping the bottom of the well with a p1000 pipette using ice-cold Basic culture medium.
Collect the organoid suspension in 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 300×g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Carefully remove the medium and BME2 layers without disrupting the organoid pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of ice-cold Basic culture medium.
Mechanically disrupt the organoids by pipetting up and down using a fire-polished glass Pasteur pipet.
Centrifuge at 300×g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 1 mL of TrypLE at room temperature.
Dissociate the broken organoids by pipetting up and down using a fire-polished glass Pasteur pipet.
Once a single cell suspension is formed, immediately add 10 mL of ice-cold Basic culture medium and keep on ice.
Centrifuge at 300×g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 250 μL ice-cold FACS buffer.
Pass the suspension through a 35 μm cell strainer.
Keep cells on ice and immediately proceed to cell sorting using a platform of choice.
